;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**The [[Israel Defense Forces]] arrest a suspected [[Hamas]] member caught tampering with equipment at the [[Karni Crossing]] on the [[Israel]]i-[[Gaza Strip|G]]azan border. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israeli-army-arrests-palestinian-tampering-with-gaza-border-1.6034131 (Haaretz)]
**An Israeli military officer states IDF snipers are targeting the legs of protestors and deaths are largely the unintentional result of protestors bending over, missing shots, and the subsequent rounds ricocheting from intended targets. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/.premium-israeli-officer-most-killings-during-gaza-protests-unintentional-1.6034421 (Haaretz)]
**A [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] youth is shot and injured at the border near [[al-Awdeh]] after approaching the border fence. [http://english.wafa.ps/page.aspx?id=0rcHCda97469976483a0rcHCd (W.A.F.A.)]
**In response to a [[Yesh Din]] petition to the Israeli [[High Court]] calling for a ban on the use of live rounds to prevent protestors breaching the border fence, the Israeli government says its [[rules of engagement]] meet local and international law, that intelligence used to justify decisions will be submitted to the court, and that the protests are considered part of the ongoing conflict with [[Hamas]]. [https://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-5245292,00.html (Ynetnews)]
**[[Amnesty International]] makes a fresh call for an arms embargo against Israel, claiming "malicious tactics" and "murderous" attacks on Gazan civilians justify one. [https://www.jpost.com/Arab-Israeli-Conflict/Amnesty-International-renews-call-for-arms-embargo-against-Israel-552986 (The Jerusalem Post)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War]]
**The [[Syrian Army]], along with what is believed to be [[Iranian involvement in the Syrian Civil War|Iranian-backed]] militias, took control villages east of the [[Euphrates|Euphrates river]] near the city of [[Deir ez-Zor]] that were under the control by [[Kurds|Kurdish]]-led forces in a rare clash with the [[Syrian Democratic Forces]]. The territory was later recaptured by U.S.-backed forces in a counter-attack spearheaded by the [[People's Protection Units|YPG]] with help from U.S.-led coalition jets that took off from American bases in northern Syria. The U.S. military says in a statement that the "coalition used established deconfliction channels to de-escalate the situation".  [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-euphrates/u-s-backed-forces-say-they-regain-villages-seized-by-syrian-army-idUSKBN1I00EX (Reuters)]
**[[Syria]]n state media, [[Syrian Arab News Agency]], reports missile strikes have targeted military sites in the [[Hama Governorate]] and [[Aleppo Governorate]]. It is unclear who carried out the strikes. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-04/30/c_137146068.htm (Xinhuanet)]

;Business and economy
*[[T-Mobile US]] and [[Sprint Corporation|Sprint]] agree to merge in a deal valued at [[United States dollar|US$]]146 billion. The merger is subject to approval from regulators. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/news/2018/04/29/t-mobile-sprint-agree-merger-americas-national-wireless-carriers-shrink-4-3/798608001/ (USA Today)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A truck collides with a bus in [[Mandsaur]], [[Madhya Pradesh]], [[India]], killing at least seven people with at least 25 more injured. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-04/29/c_137145408.htm (Xinhua)]
*A fire in a [[circuit board]] factory in [[Taoyuan City]], [[Taiwan]], kills seven people including five firefighters. It is the city's third major industrial fire this year. [http://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2018/apr/29/five-firefighters-among-7-dead-in-taiwan-factory-blaze-1807935.html (The New Indian Express)]

;International relations
*[[2017–18 North Korea crisis]]
**South Korean officials say that [[North Korea]]n leader [[Kim Jong-un]] stated during his [[April 2018 inter-Korean summit|summit]] meeting with [[South Korea]]n [[President of South Korea|President]] [[Moon Jae-in]] that he would close the country's [[Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site]] in May. [http://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/2143878/north-korea-close-mountain-nuclear-test-site-after-collapse (SCMP)]
**[[South Korea]] stated that Kim is willing to give up his nuclear weapons if the United States vows not to attack. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/korea-close-nuke-test-site-unify-time-zone-54806870 (ABC News)]
*[[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]]
**The leaders of the [[United Kingdom]], [[Germany]] and [[France]] agree on their support for the Iran nuclear deal as the best way to prevent Iran from having nuclear weapons. [http://thehill.com/policy/international/385399-uk-france-germany-join-together-to-support-iran-deal (''The Hill'')]
**[[United States Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] says the United States will quit the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|agreement]] if its "flaws" can't be fixed. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-04-29/pompeo-urges-gulf-unity-in-apparent-attempt-to-end-qatar-spat (Bloomberg)]
**A member of [[Iran]]'s [[Expediency Discernment Council |Expediency Council]] calls on the [[European Union]], [[Russia]] and [[China]] to support the deal and guarantee [[Economy|economic]] and [[bank]]ing relations with Iran. He warns that Iran would likely exit the deal if it doesn't benefit Iran. [http://www.tehrantimes.com/news/423121/Iran-would-abandon-barren-nuclear-deal-official-warns (''Tehran Times'')]

;Law and crime
*In [[Newport, Wales]] McCauley Cox [[Vehicle-ramming attack | drove his car into a crowd]] outside a nightclub and intentionally hit and injured 4 people before he fled the scene. He claimed he was trying to stop a fight but was found guilty and sentenced for  causing grievous bodily harm with intent, causing serious injury through dangerous driving and causing actual bodily harm. Teens Benjamin Thomas and Callum Banton pleaded guilty to affray for their part in starting the brawl which preceded the attack. [https://www.southwalesargus.co.uk/news/16308245.teens-jailed-for-fight-in-cambrian-road-newport-before-car-hit-pedestrians/ (South Wales Argus)] 
*A bomb explodes outside the Arun III Hydroelectric Power Plant in [[Tumlingtar]], [[Nepal]]. No group claimed credit for the attack. The plant was codeveloped with [[India]] and is due to be inaugurated by [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] within weeks. [http://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2018/apr/29/bomb-blast-at-nepals-hydroelectricity-projects-office-weeks-before-inauguration-by-narendra-modi-1807910.html (The New Indian Express)]
*The [[Central Criminal Court of Iraq|Central Criminal Court]] in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]], sentences nineteen [[Russia]]n women, six [[Azerbaijan]]i women, and four [[Tajikistan]]i women to life in prison for membership to [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]. [https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/world/2018-04-29-iraq-sentences-19-russian-women-to-life-for-joining-islamic-state/ (The Sunday Times)]
*The [[Israel Defense Forces]] detain one of two [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] shepherds who they say crossed the [[United Nations]]-patrolled border between the two nations. Lebanon calls the detention an "abduction". The IDF says the female shepherd, detained in the disputed [[Shebaa]] region, was quickly repatriated. [https://www.jpost.com/Arab-Israeli-Conflict/Lebanese-army-says-Israel-abducted-citizen-on-border-552994 (The Jerusalem Post)]
* A police operation in nine commercial premises of the district of [[La Victoria District, Lima|La Victoria]], in [[Lima]], Peru, managed to seize two tons of pharmaceutical and natural products with an expired shelf life, without sanitary registration, and allegedly falsified. The police officers in charge of this raid on informed that now they will continue to find the whereabouts of all the people involved in the commercialization of this merchandise. [https://peru21.pe/lima/victoria-policia-incauto-2-toneladas-medicinas-productos-naturales-adulterados-video-405173?foto=5 (''Perú 21'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Amber Rudd]] resigns as the [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Home Secretary]] amid controversy over the threatened deportation of [[Windrush generation]] immigrants. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-43944988 (BBC)]

;Sports
*[[Brazil]] surfer Rodrigo Koxa breaks the record for the largest wave ever surfed. The wave occurred off the coast of Nazaré, Portugal and measured 24.4 meters (80 feet). [https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-europe-43942906/brazilian-surfer-rodrigo-koxa-breaks-wave-world-record (BBC)]
